---
title: "017 — Section peek strip"
---

> **Status:** standing (an owner ruling moved it from per-reply bars to a page-level
> tick gutter within days of merge, before 0.6.0 shipped)

**Goal.** Give long, header-structured replies an at-a-glance map and a
two-interaction path into any section, with no permanent screen chrome: a hairline
strip along the reply's edge, one bar per section sized by its share of the reply; hover
fattens the bars into a readable map; a deliberate ~400 ms dwell pops a plain-text
preview of the section's opening lines; clicking bar or preview scrolls the transcript
so the heading lands at the viewport's top. The qualification gate keeps it quiet:
finished streaming, at least three sections, taller than a viewport — short replies show
nothing. A persisted settings toggle turns it off entirely; touch input skips the dwell
and taps to jump; scrolling, text selection, expound highlighting, and copy behave
identically with the strip present.

**Why.** This spec is the winner of the `ideas/003-chat-outline` deck
— Card 006, hover-peek bars — dealt as a six-card deck and played on September 2. The
card was born mid-playthrough, out of the user's own distraction worry about the
runner-up floating panel ([015 — floating reply outline](015-floating-reply-outline.qmd)):
a near-invisible rest state answers the objection permanent chrome could not. The
verdict kept the panel as the recorded upgrade path and carried the card's snags into
the spec as design requirements — hover-intent tuning, preview freshness (cache
plain-text excerpts, refresh on edit or regenerate), a touch fallback, generous hit
targets, and registering the strip's selectors with the expound exclusion list.

**Outcome & reversals.** Specced and shipped in a day (merged September 2, PR #16):
pure mdast extraction — real headings only, with code, callouts, tables, and math
excluded by construction; a pure dwell state machine testable without timers; a
sole-writer preference module with defensive reads; jump orchestration in the chat page
(nth-heading resolution with rAF retry for far-unmounted replies, stick-to-bottom
suppression, reduced-motion honor, no URL writes); source-contract tests pinning pointer
discipline and the streaming gate; and the toggle housed in a new Chat section of
014's settings registry. Review fixes tightened callout-safe jump anchors and preview
anchoring; browser validation and the perf probe closed all 22 tasks. Then the owner
reversed the topology before release: the strip left the message wrapper for a
page-level gutter outside the transcript's scroll container — thin left-aligned ticks
whose widths encode section share, scroll-synced, with the preview floating outside the
chat area and a wheel relay keeping scrolling whole across the sibling boundary. The
rewrite also replaced per-message reactive wiring with a context-provided registry
after a plain array triggered a 32-second flush storm, and a mock-LLM fixture with
deliberately duplicated headings joined the e2e suite; the 0.6.0 notes describe the
tick form. Throughout, the feature deliberately consumed 015's contract rather than
forking it — extraction, jump-plus-flash, and the exclusion-list rule are that design's
primitives realized — and the where-am-I position marker was deferred as the recorded
bridge to the floating panel.

**Learnings.**

- A near-invisible rest state is what makes navigation chrome acceptable; the
  distraction objection has nothing left to hold onto.
- Pure transition functions make pointer intent testable — no timers, no DOM in the
  test.
- Injected text-bearing chrome must join the selection-alignment exclusion list at
  design time, not after the first misaligned highlight.
- Reactive arrays over per-message DOM state can storm; a version-counter registry is
  the cheap cure.
- Defer the upgrade seam explicitly: the marker that would become the floating panel is
  one decision away, and the record says so.
